sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.4 'Hlepho Phowa phonology in brief' (pp. 9-10) gives syllable template {(C)(V)VT}, segment inventory, four tonemes /55 33 13 21/ and sandhi; sec. 4.7 'The Phowa meso-clade' (pp. 16-17) mentions Labo Phowa [ypb] only for tone-class reflexes and shared lexical innovations. No occurrence of 'stress'/'accent' anywhere in the text. Describes the sister lect Hlepho Phowa, not Labo; refers to Pelkey 2011 (De Gruyter) pp. 223-270 for full sketches.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2005. Puzzling over Phula: Toward the Synthesis and Statement of a Sub-Branch. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 28(2): 43-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 6.1 'Ani Phowa: a newly described Phula variety' (pp. 58-60): 42 consonant initials, 11 vowel finals, five tonal contrasts (high, mid, low, low-rising, low-falling), tense-lax phonation. 'stress(es)' occurs only in the ordinary-language sense (pp. 48, 50). Describes Ani Phowa [ypn], sister lect, not Labo.
